summary: COSMOSCOPE is a browser-based personal universe laboratory that allows users to create their own planet according to parameters like radius, mass, atmosphere, star and orbit. The planet will change in real-time 3D visualizations of the created planet, while providing scientific profiles of the planet, such as surface gravity, escape velocity, equilibrium temperature, atmospheric retention, position within the habitable zone and the Earth Similarity Index. Users can also compare their planet to existing planets within the exoplanet catalog. The website features six modules: Planet Creator, Exoplanet Explorer, Solar System Live, Cosmic Experiments, Space Detective and Scientific Missions. Each calculation includes the formula used and the limits of the model. COSMOSCOPE is available in five languages. This website was developed to make the science behind NASA's exoplanet discoveries understandable and playable for students and the general public around the world.
details:
What it does: COSMOSCOPE is a web lab that allows users to explore planets inside and beyond our Solar System. The website contains six modules that are all connected.

Planet Creator: Set parameters for your planet, such as radius, mass, atmosphere, host star and orbit and see how it changes in 3D space with a live scientific profile.

Exoplanet Explorer: Browse through a catalog of real exoplanets, such as TRAPPIST-1e, Proxima b, Kepler-452b and others and compare them to Earth. You can also open any of these planets within the Planet Creator app.

Solar System: The eight planets in our Solar System will move along their real orbits, computed from JPL orbital elements, at adjustable speeds.

Cosmic Experiments: State a hypothesis regarding some phenomenon in space and let the simulation engine test it for you.

Space Detective: Identify a real exoplanet from the measurements that astronomers have made of it.

Scientific Missions: Six different scientific missions with targets and badges to earn.

How it works. All values are computed live in the browser from physics: mass - radius relation (Chen & Kipping 2017), surface gravity, escape velocity, equilibrium temperature with a greenhouse model, atmospheric retention, habitable-zone limits (Kopparapu et al. 2013) and Earth Similarity Index. Each calculation shows its formula and its limits.

Impact. The website transforms data from NASA missions like Kepler, TESS, Hubble and Webb into hands-on experiments that allow students and the general public to learn about habitability and the scientific method, in five languages (EN, ES, FR, JA, RU).

Tools. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (WebGL) and SVG. Built with AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic).

Creativity & considerations. Users do not simply browse data. Instead, users create their own worlds and test them against the scientific principles of the habitability of those planets. The habitability score of each planet is listed as a teaching tool for the website, the artist's impressions of each planet are listed as illustrative of the data and the website can be accessed from mobile devices.
